- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥1.0) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% relative to historical mean or recent peak.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots in next 3–5 days; apply downward correction of 3–8% to avoid overreaction.
- If sentiment is neutral or negative (0.0) and price is trending downward, model frequently underestimates the drop; adjust forecast downward by 1–4% to reflect mean reversion bias.
- Model tends to lag in early periods (e.g., first 5–7 days of forecast) when sentiment is volatile; apply slight upward bias to compensate for lag.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overpredicts mid-term recovery after downturns; cap forecast at 10–15% below recent 14-day high to avoid overconfidence in rebound.
- When sentiment shifts from negative to positive, model delays correction; add 1–3 days of lagged sentiment influence to forecast adjustment.
